title: Counting the Days a Storage Charge Has Stood Past Its Grace Period
content:
The days a charge has stood past its grace period are counted by the way the member's statements reach them, since when a charge becomes visible to the member differs by channel. This rule governs Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Basis of the charge

Where statements reach the member through the portal and by email, the grace period is counted in whole calendar days from the date storage was last billed and paid through, since a charge is there to be seen the day it is raised.

Where statements reach the member by post, the same count is taken and the posting allowance of 5 calendar days is added to the grace period.

And otherwise the grace period is counted in whole calendar days from the day the most recent storage charge was raised on the account.

## The channel and the grace period by programme

| Programme | Statements reach the member by | Grace period (calendar days) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | counter printout | 15 |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | mailed statement | 15 |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | mailed statement | 10 |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | email statement | 10 |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | portal and email | 10 |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | portal and email | 10 |

The middle line of the clause is the postal channel alone. A counter printout and an email statement both fall to the closing line, where the count runs from the day the most recent storage charge was raised on the account rather than from the date storage was last billed and paid through.

## Condition, count and allowance

| Statements reach the member | The days are counted from | Days allowed before a charge stands past grace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| through the portal and by email | the date storage was last billed and paid through | the programme's grace period |
| by post | the date storage was last billed and paid through | the programme's grace period and a further 5 days |
| by any other channel | the day the most recent storage charge was raised on the account | the programme's grace period |

Where the count does not exceed the days allowed, no charge stands past its grace period at all.

## Worked counts, on hypothetical dates

Take a charge worked out on 20 June on a programme whose grace period is 10 calendar days, with the date storage was last billed and paid through standing at 1 June and the most recent storage charge raised on 14 June.

**Statements through the portal and by email.** From 1 June to 20 June is 19 days; less the grace period of 10, the charge stands 9 days past grace.

**Statements by post.** The same 19 days, less the grace period of 10 and the posting allowance of 5, leaves the charge 4 days past grace.

**Statements by counter printout.** From 14 June to 20 June is 6 days; less the grace period of 10 that is below nothing, so no charge stands past its grace period.
